title: Time Allocation
hook: I was busy all week and moved nothing that actually mattered. Busy isn't the same as productive.
statement: How you spend your hours is how your business and life turn out. Your calendar shows your real priorities.
explainer: You can say growth is the priority, but if your hours go to admin and inbox, that's your actual priority. Weighting time by importance shows the truth.
sop: Track every hour for one full week.
Give each activity a Priority Weight from 1 to 3.
Multiply Time by Priority Weight for each and add them up.
Find the big-time, low-weight activities. Those are your leaks.
Rebuild next week so more hours go to your weight 3 work.
equation_example: Task A: 3 hours × weight 3 = 9. Task B: 5 hours × weight 1 = 5. Total 9 + 5 = 14. B took more time but scored less. Higher means your hours go to what matters. Lower means busy work is winning.
question: Open your calendar and circle the hours that don't match what you say matters most.
closing_statement: A full calendar isn't the same as a good one.
caption:
Principle Nº 154: Time Allocation

I was busy all week and moved nothing that actually mattered. Busy isn't the same as productive.

How you spend your hours is how your business and life turn out. Your calendar shows your real priorities.

Your turn: Open your calendar and circle the hours that don't match what you say matters most.
